reason: I want to prepare the local material for paving, and shoveling at the workshop ground seems like a natural place to start.
expectation: I expect to collect or expose some local material, though I don't know whether it will be ready for paving.

alternatives.reason: The mesh and metal stock might make a useful screen, but I want to see what material is available first.

effect: The excavation produced regolith, giving me local material to prepare for paving.
reaction: That result was straightforward; I’m curious how the material will be processed.
reason: The mesh and metal stock are the only available combination, and they may make a screen for the excavated regolith.
expectation: I expect to make some kind of screening tool, although its exact use is uncertain.

effect: The mesh and stock made a sieve, giving me a way to sort the excavated regolith.
reaction: That was a predictable but satisfying construction.
reason: Sieving the regolith is the only available combination and seems like a natural preparation for making paving.
expectation: I expect the sieve to separate finer material from larger particles, though I don't know which portion the paving will use.

effect: Sieving produced a consistent fine feedstock for a furnace trial, explaining why grading matters.
reaction: The explanation makes the preparation feel purposeful; I’m curious what the furnace will produce.
reason: The furnace trial is the only available combination and is the next step toward making paving.
expectation: I expect the furnace to heat the graded regolith into a useful paving material, though the result is uncertain.

effect: The slower furnace cycle produced porous bricks suitable for a floor and other structures, and the goal now calls for laying the workshop floor.
reaction: The failed edge and slower retry made the firing process more interesting, especially the distinction that the bricks need not hold an atmosphere.
reason: Placing the bricks at the workshop ground directly addresses the new goal of making a solid floor.
expectation: I expect the bricks to be laid as workshop paving, though I don't know whether another preparation will be needed.

alternatives.reason: The metal stock might help make a support or another structure, but the workshop ground is the clearer match for the floor goal.

effect: The bricks became workshop paving, completing the solid floor and the chapter.
reaction: A straightforward, satisfying finish to the sequence.

mostWorthwhile.text: The furnace trial was most worthwhile: the failed edge and slower successful cycle showed why processing conditions matter, while explaining the bricks’ structural limits.

leastWorthwhile.text: Excavating the regolith was the least interesting passage; it was a straightforward collection step with no explanation at that point.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the first firing trial flaked and a slower cycle produced sound bricks, and that their intended uses did not require them to hold an atmosphere.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary. The reason for making the sieve became clear when it produced consistent feedstock for the furnace trial.

continue.text: I would continue: the practical explanations of grading and firing made me curious how the other possible brick structures might be used.
